trust_decision.summary: An admin-supplied monitor expectedValue is compiled as a backtracking JS RegExp and run against the remote HTTP response body on every check in the worker; the fix decides that only RE2-compatible (linear-time) patterns may be compiled, both at check time (AdvancedMatcher) and at save time (zod superRefine on create/edit/import schemas).

landing_point.why: The summary names 'Monitor Advanced Matching' with a user-controlled regex; the only `new RegExp(expected)` in the server is in AdvancedMatcher.compare.

fix_sites.entry_point: Worker HTTP check of any stored http monitor with useAdvancedMatching (HttpProvider.buildResponse -> advancedMatcher.validate), fed by POST /monitors, PATCH /monitors/:monitorId, POST /monitors/import/json

fix_sites.module_kind: zod request schema (bulk import / export round-trip)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: server/src/api/validation/monitorValidation.ts:185-235 (importedMonitorSchema, used by POST /monitors/import/json at server/src/api/routes/monitorRoute.ts:49); also patterns already stored in MongoDB (server/src/domain/monitors/monitor.model.ts:263-269 has no regex check) are only covered by the runtime change

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Import is an admin-only restore of previously exported monitors, so a solver can argue its data was already validated at create time; a solver who fixes only the create/edit schemas leaves stored and imported patterns running through native RegExp in the worker.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate regex matching must keep working (e.g. `^2\d{2}$` against an extracted status code), and so must the equal/include methods and the empty-expectedValue falsy check. Over-broad fixes (escaping the pattern, dropping the regex method, rejecting all quantifiers) break this.

O6_input_shapes: expectedValue as a plain string on create/edit/import bodies
extracted JMESPath value of any JSON type (object/array/number) coerced with String() before matching (fix.diff:53-58)
invalid or RE2-unsupported pattern (backreferences/lookaround) -> 'Invalid regex pattern' instead of a throw (fix.diff:64-68, fix.diff:101-111)

O7_producer.where: server/src/api/validation/monitorValidation.ts:107,141,200 (expectedValue accepted as any string); persisted via server/src/domain/monitors/monitor.repository.mongo.ts:274-283 and read back at server/src/domain/monitors/monitor.repository.mongo.ts:548

O8_uncovered_routes.route: PATCH /monitors/:monitorId with only matchMethod='regex' (or only expectedValue) in the body. The added refineRegexPattern returns early unless both fields are in the same body, and the repository $sets the partial patch onto the stored value, so the save-time check is bypassed. The runtime RE2 change still covers the sink.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The runtime matcher already uses RE2, so the save-time check is only UX; and PATCH semantics are 'validate what you send'.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: validation file -> domain repository, same server package

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A header- or status-message matcher, or a second provider (e.g. a geo-check or JSON body provider) that reuses a copy of compare() with native RegExp
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Providers are pluggable (IStatusProvider) and a maintainer adding matching to another monitor type would plausibly copy the old compare() helper.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An import/duplicate path that builds monitors from data the fixed zod schema never parses (e.g. a CSV import or a 'duplicate monitor' service call)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: importMonitorsFromJSON already maps unvalidated-looking objects into createMonitors; a duplicate or template feature would naturally bypass the request schema.

O9_family: ReDoS (CWE-1333): user-controlled pattern compiled by a backtracking regex engine

O10_build.toolchain: npm, tsc, jest (ESM via --experimental-vm-modules); the fix adds the native 're2' addon, which is not a dependency at the pinned commit
services: MongoDB (for full API/worker; not needed for AdvancedMatcher/zod unit tests)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a zod refine on POST /monitors that rejects 'dangerous' regexes, or wrap new RegExp in try/catch or a length cap, leaving the native backtracking engine running in the worker for stored, imported and PATCHed patterns.
